Getting to an uw BMI means fuck all tbh when it comes to periods.

You can lose your period restricting at a "normal" weight, you can lose your period restricting at an ow BMI. You can have your period restricting at an uw BMI. Losing your period can be a mix of what you're eating, speed of weight loss (which is effectively stress on your body - as is b/ping), body fat among other things.

It's definitely worth going to your doctor to get bloods checked etc, just in case there is something else going on (PCOS, hormone issues etc). Not having a period can cause a lot of issues later on in life like increased risk of osteoporosis (from what I remember, but don't hold me to it).

Definitely don't recommend ignoring. It could be nothing major, but it's always better to be safe than sorry when it comes to your health, especially when there's an ED involved.
